name: Chapter 12: Kinetic Theory
description: Molecular nature of matter, gas laws, pressure of an ideal gas, kinetic interpretation of temperature, rms speed, equipartition, specific heats, mean free path

cards.term: What is the basic idea of kinetic theory?
cards.definition: A gas is made of rapidly moving molecules with negligible interactions except during collisions

cards.term: Who developed kinetic theory, and what does it explain?
cards.definition: Maxwell, Boltzmann and others (19th century): pressure, temperature, gas laws, Avogadro’s hypothesis, specific heats, viscosity, diffusion

cards.term: State Feynman’s "atomic hypothesis".
cards.definition: All things are made of atoms in perpetual motion, attracting when a little apart and repelling when squeezed together

cards.term: Ancient atomic ideas: who in India and Greece?
cards.definition: Kanada (Vaiseshika school, ~6th century BC; paramanu) and Democritus (4th century BC; "atom" = indivisible)

cards.term: Who is credited with the scientific atomic theory, and which laws did it explain?
cards.definition: John Dalton: laws of definite and multiple proportions

cards.term: State Gay Lussac’s law and Avogadro’s law.
cards.definition: Gay Lussac: reacting gas volumes are in small-integer ratios. Avogadro: equal volumes of gases at the same T and P have the same number of molecules

cards.term: Molecular sizes and spacings
cards.definition: Size of an atom: ≈ 1 Å (10⁻¹⁰ m); Spacing in solids and liquids: ≈ 2 Å; Spacing in gases: tens of Å; Mean free path in gases: thousands of Å

cards.term: Why is a gas at equilibrium called a dynamic equilibrium?
cards.definition: Molecules keep colliding and changing speeds; only average properties stay constant

cards.term: Ideal gas equation in terms of molecules?
cards.definition: \( PV = Nk_BT \), or \( P = nk_BT \) (n = number density); k = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹

cards.term: Relation between R, k and Nₐ?
cards.definition: \( R = N_A k_B \) = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹

cards.term: Ideal gas equation in terms of density?
cards.definition: \[P = \dfrac{\rho RT}{M_0}\](M₀ = molar mass)

cards.term: Molar volume at STP? Avogadro number?
cards.definition: 22.4 L at 273 K and 1 atm; 6.02 × 10²³ molecules

cards.term: When does a real gas behave ideally?
cards.definition: At low pressure and high temperature (molecules far apart, interactions negligible)

cards.term: Boyle’s law and Charles’ law from PV = μRT?
cards.definition: Fix μ, T: PV = constant. Fix P: V ∝ T

cards.term: How do experimental T–V curves of CO₂ compare with Charles’ law?
cards.definition: They agree at low pressure; deviate more at high pressure

cards.term: Dalton’s law of partial pressures?
cards.definition: \[P = P_1 + P_2 + \dots\]each Pᵢ = μᵢRT/V as if that gas alone filled the vessel

cards.term: Example 12.1: water density 1000 kg/m³, vapour at 100 °C 0.6 kg/m³. Fraction of vapour volume occupied by molecules?
cards.definition: ≈ 6 × 10⁻⁴

cards.term: Example 12.2: estimate the size of a water molecule.
cards.definition: Mass = 0.018/(6 × 10²³) = 3 × 10⁻²⁶ kg → volume 3 × 10⁻²⁹ m³ → radius ≈ 2 Å

cards.term: Example 12.3: average distance between molecules in water vapour?
cards.definition: Volume grows ~10³ ×, spacing ~10 × radius → ≈ 40 Å

cards.term: Example 12.4: Ne and O₂ with partial pressures 3 : 2. Ratio of molecules and of mass densities?
cards.definition: Molecules 3 : 2; densities (3/2)(20.2/32.0) = 0.947

cards.term: Exercise 12.2: show molar volume at STP is 22.4 L.
Exercise 12.3: PV/T vs P for 1.00 g of O₂. Meaning of the dotted line, and the common intercept?
cards.definition: Dotted = ideal gas intercept = μR = (1/32) × 8.31 = 0.26 J/K T₁ > T₂ (closer to ideal)

cards.term: Exercise 12.4: 30 L O₂ cylinder, gauge 15 atm at 27 °C falls to 11 atm at 17 °C. Mass taken out?
cards.definition: ≈ 0.14 kg (use absolute pressures 16 and 12 atm)

cards.term: Exercise 12.5: 1.0 cm³ bubble rises from 40 m depth (12 °C) to the surface (35 °C). New volume?
cards.definition: ≈ 5.3 cm³ (P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂)

cards.term: Exercise 12.6: molecules in a 25.0 m³ room at 27 °C and 1 atm?
cards.definition: N = PV/kT ≈ 6.1 × 10²⁶

cards.term: Assumptions of kinetic theory of gases
cards.definition: Molecules: huge number, in random motion; Size: negligible vs distances between them; Forces: none except during collisions; Collisions: elastic, very short

cards.term: Momentum given to a wall when a molecule rebounds elastically?
Pressure of an ideal gas from kinetic theory
cards.definition: Momentum 2mvx per hit, ½ nAvxΔt hits → P = nm⟨vx²⟩ = ⅓ nm⟨v²⟩

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
12.4.1 · pressure of an ideal gas

Find the missing step.

Derive P = ⅓ nm⟨v²⟩ for a gas in a box.
  1. Each hit gives the wall 2mvₓ
  2. ?
  3. P = nm⟨vₓ²⟩
  4. Isotropy: ⟨vₓ²⟩ = ⟨v²⟩/3 → P = ⅓ nm⟨v²⟩
advancedHtml.backHtml:
12.4.1 · pressure of an ideal gas

Find the missing step.

Derive P = ⅓ nm⟨v²⟩ for a gas in a box.
  1. Each hit gives the wall 2mvₓ
  2. In time Δt, ½ nAvₓΔt molecules hit area A
  3. P = nm⟨vₓ²⟩
  4. Isotropy: ⟨vₓ²⟩ = ⟨v²⟩/3 → P = ⅓ nm⟨v²⟩

cards.term: Why doesn’t the container’s shape or molecular collisions spoil the pressure formula?
cards.definition: Pressure is the same everywhere (Pascal); collisions just swap velocities in a steady distribution

cards.term: Pressure in terms of kinetic energy?
cards.definition: \[PV = \tfrac23 E\](E = total translational KE)

cards.term: Kinetic interpretation of temperature?
cards.definition: \[\tfrac12 m\langle v^2\rangle = \tfrac32 k_BT\]average translational KE per molecule ∝ T, independent of P, V and the gas

cards.term: Internal energy of an ideal gas depends on…?
cards.definition: Temperature only (E = 3/2 NkT for monatomic)

cards.term: Define rms speed. Formula?
cards.definition: \[v_{rms} = \sqrt{\langle v^2\rangle} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3k_BT}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M_0}}\]

cards.term: rms speed of N₂ at 300 K?
cards.definition: ≈ 516 m/s — about the speed of sound

cards.term: At the same temperature, which molecules are faster?
cards.definition: The lighter ones (vᵣₘₛ ∝ 1/√m)

cards.term: Trap: is ⟨v²⟩ equal to ⟨v⟩²?
cards.definition: Not in general: the mean of squares exceeds the square of the mean (e.g. speeds 1 and 3: ⟨v²⟩ = 5, ⟨v⟩² = 4)

cards.term: Example 12.5: argon and chlorine (2 : 1 by mass) at 27 °C. Ratio of average KE per molecule and of rms speeds?
cards.definition: KE 1 : 1; vᵣₘₛ(Ar)/vᵣₘₛ(Cl₂) = √(70.9/39.9) = 1.33 (mass ratio irrelevant)

cards.term: Example 12.6: ²³⁵UF₆ vs ²³⁸UF₆. Which is faster and by how much?
cards.definition: ²³⁵UF₆, by √(352/349) − 1 ≈ 0.44 % — used for uranium enrichment by diffusion

cards.term: Graham’s law of diffusion (Exercise 12.12 idea)?
cards.definition: Rate of diffusion ∝ 1/√(molar mass)

cards.term: Example 12.7: why does a gas heat up when compressed by a moving piston?
cards.definition: Molecules rebound from the approaching piston faster (like a ball off a moving bat), so average KE and T rise; expansion cools it

cards.term: Exercise 12.7: average thermal energy of a helium atom at 300 K, 6000 K, 10⁷ K?
cards.definition: 6.2 × 10⁻²¹ J, 1.24 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, 2.1 × 10⁻¹⁶ J (3/2 kT)

cards.term: Exercise 12.8: equal vessels of Ne, Cl₂, UF₆ at the same T, P. Same number of molecules? Largest vᵣₘₛ?
cards.definition: Yes (Avogadro); vᵣₘₛ largest for neon (lightest)

cards.term: Exercise 12.9: at what temperature is vᵣₘₛ of argon equal to that of helium at −20 °C?
Why don’t air molecules settle on the floor?
cards.definition: Their KE (~kT) is much larger than mgh for room heights; collisions keep them spread out

cards.term: Correction: NCERT 12.4.2 begins "Equation (13.14) can be written as". Which equation?
cards.definition: Eq. (12.14), P = ⅓ nm⟨v²⟩; the number is left over from the old chapter order

cards.term: What is a degree of freedom?
cards.definition: An independent way a molecule can store energy: each squared term in its energy (½mvₓ², ½Iω², ½ky²…)

cards.term: Degrees of freedom of a monatomic and a rigid diatomic molecule?
cards.definition: Monatomic: 3 (translation). Rigid diatomic: 5 (3 translation + 2 rotation)

cards.term: Why only 2 rotational degrees for a diatomic molecule?
cards.definition: Rotation about the line joining the atoms has almost zero moment of inertia and does not come into play (quantum reasons)

cards.text: Law of equipartition: in equilibrium, each quadratic energy mode has average energy {{c1::½ kT}}; a vibrational mode contributes {{c2::kT}} (kinetic + potential).

cards.term: Who first proved the equipartition law?
cards.definition: Maxwell

cards.term: Molar specific heats from equipartition
cards.definition: Monatomic (3 dof): Cᵥ = 3R/2, Cₚ = 5R/2, γ = 5/3; Rigid diatomic (5 dof): Cᵥ = 5R/2, Cₚ = 7R/2, γ = 7/5; Diatomic with vibration: Cᵥ = 7R/2, Cₚ = 9R/2, γ = 9/7; Polyatomic, f vibrational modes: Cᵥ = (3 + f)R, Cₚ = (4 + f)R

cards.term: General shortcut: Cᵥ and γ in terms of degrees of freedom f?
cards.definition: \[C_v = \dfrac f2 R,\quad \gamma = 1 + \dfrac 2f\]

cards.term: Does Cₚ − Cᵥ = R depend on the type of gas?
cards.definition: No: true for every ideal gas

cards.term: How well do the predictions match experiment (Table 12.2)?
cards.definition: Very well for He, Ne, Ar, H₂, O₂, N₂; gases like Cl₂, C₂H₆ are higher because vibrations are active

cards.term: Example 12.8: 44.8 L cylinder of helium at STP heated by 15 °C at constant volume. Heat needed?
cards.definition: 2 mol × (3/2)R × 15 = 45R ≈ 374 J

cards.term: Molar specific heat of solids from equipartition?
cards.definition: Each atom: 3D oscillator, energy 3kT → U = 3RT per mole → C = 3R (carbon is an exception)

cards.term: Why does leaking cooking gas take a long time to spread though molecules move at ~500 m/s?
cards.definition: Molecules keep colliding; their paths zig-zag

cards.term: Define mean free path.
cards.definition: Average distance a molecule travels between successive collisions

cards.term: Formula for mean free path?
cards.definition: \[l = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt2\,n\pi d^2}\](n = number density, d = molecular diameter)

cards.term: Why the √2 in the mean free path formula?
cards.definition: The other molecules also move; the relative velocity sets the collision rate

cards.term: Mean free path and collision time for air at STP?
cards.definition: l ≈ 2.9 × 10⁻⁷ m (~1500 d); τ ≈ 6 × 10⁻¹⁰ s

cards.term: How does mean free path depend on pressure and temperature?
cards.definition: \[l \propto \dfrac1n = \dfrac{kT}{P}\]larger at low pressure (vacuum tubes) and high temperature

cards.term: Example 12.9: mean free path of water vapour at 373 K?
cards.definition: l scales with T: 2.9 × 10⁻⁷ × 373/273 ≈ 4 × 10⁻⁷ m — ~100 × the intermolecular distance

cards.term: Exercise 12.10: N₂ at 2.0 atm, 17 °C, radius 1.0 Å. Mean free path and collision frequency?
cards.definition: l ≈ 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ m frequency ≈ 5 × 10⁹ s⁻¹ free time ≈ 500 × collision time

cards.term: Exercise 12.1: fraction of volume occupied by O₂ molecules at STP (d = 3 Å)?
cards.definition: ≈ 4 × 10⁻⁴

cards.term: Chapter 12 formula sheet
cards.definition: Pressure: P = ⅓ nm⟨v²⟩; Average KE per molecule: (3/2) kT; rms speed: √(3RT/M₀); Energy per quadratic mode: ½ kT; Mean free path: 1/(√2 nπd²)
